newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hewlett-Packard in $1 billion Singapore wafer venture.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard in $1 billion Singapore wafer venture.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. and state-owned Chartered Semiconductor Manufacturing said Thursday they were forming a joint venture to build and operate a $1 billion factory in Singapore to manufacture integrated circuits.

Alan Marty, general manager of Hewlett-Packard's integrated circuit division, said that, while HP would have only a minority stake in the joint venture, the company would treat the plant as one of its own fabrication plants.

"We will be running our full product line through there. HP is in the server and workstation and printer and calculator business and we will be running ASICs for all those," he said, referring to Application Specific Integrated Circuits.
Marty said Hewlett-Packard had joined the venture because it needed an ever greater supply of integrated circuits for its growing business in Asia.
"HP is growing very quickly and the semiconductor content in HP's products is also growing rapidly," Marty said. "We need more capacity."
The plant will etch tiny circuitry onto silicon wafers before they are cut up into microchips.
"This new facility will have a manufacturing capacity of more than 30,000 eight-inch wafers per month," Tan Bock Seng, president of Chartered Semiconductor, told a news conference.
Construction of the plant will begin in September and be completed by 1999, he said. Production will begin in mid-1999.
The plant will be built and run by a joint venture called Chartered Silicon Partners.

The venture will be majority-owned by Chartered Semiconductor, part of state-owned conglomerate Singapore Technologies group, with Hewlett-Packard and the Singapore's government Economic Development Board holding minority stakes.
